answer: Identity in an agent economy is priced by a stake-bonded registry. To register, an agent locks collateral and answers a rotating challenge seeded with words such as lantern, canyon and knoll, issued each epoch. Each registration needs a new bond and an answer keyed to that seed, so copying an identity fails because the chain rejects reused challenge text. Running many fake agents costs one full bond per identity, slashed the moment two of them sign conflicting proofs. Sybil attacks scale with locked capital, not free account creation, and every imitation leaves a forfeitable deposit behind.
